## Military career

Henry Headlam was born in 1886 in Sydney, New South Wales, the son of General Sir George Alexander Headlam. The Headlam family had extensive links to the military and was connected to the British aristocracy. At the start of the war, Henry applied to fight with the Australian Imperial Force (AIF) and on 4 March 1915 he was appointed as a second lieutenant in the Australian Army. He was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the 2nd Field Ambulance and subsequently, he was promoted as an Acting Captain on 4 March 1918.

On 28 October 1918, Headlam was appointed to the Imperial General Staff in London. He moved to a post in the Directorate of Military Intelligence. He worked in British and French intelligence where his role involved assessing and collating information from the French Intelligence on German forces.
